name: Spider-Man
description: Web-slinging wisdom from Peter Parker, Miles Morales, and everyone who shaped them, across Marvel's live-action films and the animated Spider-Verse.
author: Quips Editorial

quotes.content: Remember, with great power comes great responsibility.
quotes.notes: Uncle Ben's last conversation with Peter, and the line that has defined every Spider-Man story since.

quotes.content: Who am I? You sure you want to know? The story of my life is not for the faint of heart.
quotes.notes: The opening narration that begins Sam Raimi's trilogy.

quotes.content: Whatever life holds in store for me, I will never forget these words: with great power comes great responsibility. This is my gift, my curse. Who am I? I'm Spider-Man.
quotes.notes: Peter's closing narration, answering the question his opening narration asked.

quotes.content: You do too much: college, a job, all this time with me. You're not Superman, you know.
quotes.notes: Aunt May worrying over a nephew who is, in fact, roughly Superman.

quotes.content: In spite of everything you've done for them, eventually, they will hate you.
quotes.notes: The Green Goblin's pitch to Spider-Man, and the fear underneath every hero story in the franchise.

quotes.content: I believe there's a hero in all of us, that keeps us honest, gives us strength, makes us noble, and finally allows us to die with pride, even though sometimes we have to be steady, and give up the thing we want the most. Even our dreams.
quotes.notes: Aunt May's answer when Peter asks whether the world still needs Spider-Man.

quotes.content: The power of the sun, in the palm of my hand.
quotes.notes: Doc Ock's fusion experiment, delivered first as a scientist's dream and later as a madman's boast.

quotes.content: Intelligence is not a privilege. It's a gift. And you use it for the good of mankind.
quotes.notes: Octavius mentoring Peter before his own experiment takes him over.

quotes.content: I'm just Peter Parker. I'm Spider-Man no more. No more.
quotes.notes: Peter quitting the job, in the film's turning point.

quotes.content: Uncle Ben meant the world to us. But he wouldn't want us living one second with revenge in our hearts. It's like a poison. It can take you over.
quotes.notes: Aunt May's warning to Peter after he learns who really killed Uncle Ben.

quotes.content: It's the choices that make us what we are, and we can always choose to do what's right.
quotes.notes: The closing narration of the Raimi trilogy.

quotes.content: Did a terrible thing to you. I spent a lot of nights wishing I could take it back.
quotes.notes: Sandman's confession to Peter about the night Uncle Ben died.

quotes.content: If you could do good things for other people, you had a moral obligation to do those things. That's what's at stake here: not choice, responsibility.
quotes.notes: This film's version of the famous lesson, which never uses the word 'power' at all.

quotes.content: We all have secrets: the ones we keep, and those ones that are kept from us.
quotes.notes: Peter on the mystery of his parents' disappearance.

quotes.content: What makes life valuable is that it doesn't last forever. What makes it precious is that it ends.
quotes.notes: From Gwen's valedictorian speech, which the film later replays as her eulogy.

quotes.content: It's easy to feel hopeful on a beautiful day like today, but there will be dark days ahead.
quotes.notes: The opening of Gwen's graduation speech.

quotes.content: My wish for you is to become hope. People need that. And even if we fail, what better way is there to live?
quotes.notes: The close of Gwen's valedictorian speech to her graduating class.

quotes.content: Every day I wake up knowing that the more people I try to save, the more enemies I will make.
quotes.notes: Peter on the arithmetic of the job.

quotes.content: When you can do the things that I can, but you don't, and then the bad things happen, they happen because of you.
quotes.notes: Peter explaining himself to Tony Stark in his Queens bedroom, the MCU's restatement of the great-power creed.

quotes.content: If you're nothing without this suit, then you shouldn't have it.
quotes.notes: Tony taking the suit back after the ferry disaster, answering Peter's 'I'm nothing without this suit.'

quotes.content: Then I wanted you to be better.
quotes.notes: Tony's reply when Peter protests that he only wanted to be like him.

quotes.content: Mr. Stark, I don't feel so good.
quotes.notes: Peter's first words as the snap takes him, largely improvised by Tom Holland on set.

quotes.content: Tony was my best friend, and he was a mess. He second-guessed everything he did. The one thing that he did that he didn't second-guess was picking you.
quotes.notes: Happy reassuring Peter that he was never meant to be the next Iron Man.

quotes.content: People, they need to believe. And nowadays, they'll believe anything.
quotes.notes: Mysterio explaining the illusion business after his cover is blown.

quotes.content: It's easy to fool people when they're already fooling themselves.
quotes.notes: Beck to Peter, on why the world took a fake hero at face value.

quotes.content: Stark chose you. He made you an Avenger. I need that. The world needs that.
quotes.notes: Fury pressing a grieving teenager back into service.

quotes.content: With great power, there must also come great responsibility.
quotes.notes: May's last words to Peter, restoring the phrasing from Amazing Fantasy #15 rather than the 2002 film's.

quotes.content: You're amazing.
quotes.notes: Improvised by Tobey Maguire to Andrew Garfield's Peter, who answers that he needed to hear it.

quotes.content: I lost Gwen. She was my MJ. I couldn't save her.
quotes.notes: The three Peters comparing losses on the rooftop.

quotes.content: Be careful what you wish for, Parker.
quotes.notes: Strange's parting words before the spell erases Peter Parker from the world's memory.

quotes.content: My name is Miles Morales. I was bitten by a radioactive spider, and for like two days, I've been the one and only Spider-Man.
quotes.notes: Miles taking over the film's origin-story narration from Peter Parker.

quotes.content: It's a leap of faith. That's all it is, Miles. A leap of faith.
quotes.notes: Peter B.'s answer to how you know you're ready, paid off in the film's signature falling shot.

quotes.content: I see this spark in you. It's amazing, it's why I push you. But it's yours. Whatever you choose to do with it, you'll be great.
quotes.notes: Jefferson speaking through Miles's closed dorm door, the moment Miles finally gets control of his powers.

quotes.content: Anyone can wear the mask. You could wear the mask. If you didn't know that before, I hope you do now.
quotes.notes: Miles's closing narration, and the thesis of the whole Spider-Verse.

quotes.content: It always fits. Eventually.
quotes.notes: Stan Lee's cameo as the costume-shop owner selling Miles a Spider-Man suit that's too big.

quotes.content: Everyone keeps telling me how my story is supposed to go. Nah. I'ma do my own thing.
quotes.notes: Miles refusing the Spider-Society's rules about which losses are inevitable.

quotes.content: In every other universe, Gwen Stacy falls for Spider-Man. And in every other universe, it doesn't end well.
quotes.notes: Gwen's narration opening the film, aware she is a recurring tragedy in someone else's story.

quotes.content: Miles, there's moments in our stories that are the same for all of us. Some good. Some bad.
quotes.notes: Miguel introducing canon events, the film's argument that suffering is structural.

quotes.content: Wherever you go from here, you have to promise to take care of that little boy for me. Make sure he never forgets where he came from. And he never doubts that he's loved.
quotes.notes: Rio sending Miles off, without knowing what she's actually sending him into.

quotes.content: Go easy on the kid. He had a terrible teacher.
quotes.notes: Peter B. defending Miles to the Spider-Society, at his own expense.
